newsitem.title: UNITED ARAB EMIRATES: SOCCER-HOLDERS JAPAN CRASH OUT OF ASIAN CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HOLDERS JAPAN CRASH OUT OF ASIAN CUP.

text.p: Defending champions Japan crashed out of the Asian Cup on Sunday.
Striker Jassem Al-Houwaidi scored in each half to give Kuwait an unexpected 2-0 win over the favourites and set up an all-Arab semifinal on Wednesday.
Kuwait will now play host to the United Arab Emirates who beat Iraq 1-0 earlier on Sunday with a ''golden goal'' in extra time.
The remaining two quarter-finals on Monday see Iran tackle South Korea and Saudi Arabia take on China.
Kuwait gave a classic defensive performance, soaking up Japanese pressure for most of the match and hitting back with swift, well constructed counter-attacks.
Al-Houwaidi, the tournament's leading scorer with five goals, scored his first in the 17th minute after a Japanese defensive blunder.
Japan -- at 20 the highest ever FIFA-ranked Asian team -- took the initiative from then on but could not breach a solid Kuwaiti defence.

Awarded a free kick in the 53rd minute for Hiroshige Yanagimoto's foul against striker Bashar Abdulaziz, Kuwait turned protest into celebration when Houwaidi tucked the ball home after Japanese goalkeeper Kenichi Shimokawa had made a mess of a relatively simple save.

Earlier, the home fans had celebrated a 1-0 win over Iraq that put the UAE into the semifinals. Asian Football Confederation (AFC) officials must have been relieved because if Iraq had won they would have played Kuwait.
Kuwait had said before the tournament that it would pull out if it had to play former occupier Iraq.
Kuwaiti defender Abdel Hussain scored from a 30-metre free kick 13 minutes into ''sudden death'' extra time after a goalless 90 minutes.
His strike sent most of the 50,000 spectators inside the stadium dancing with joy while motorists across the country -- listening to the match on radio -- honked to cheer the victory.
The UAE scorned the chance to clinch the game in normal time when midfielder Bakhit Saad's weak penalty was saved by the diving Emad Hassan.
UAE goalkeeper Muhsin Fairouz kept his team in the match in the 95th minute, producing a brilliant reflex save from Khalid Sabbar's close-range shot.
